title: Translate PDFs and keep their layout
summary: PDF translation that keeps the layout, translate a whole Drive folder, folder detail pages, choose the folder for Save to Assets, export preview and a lip-sync model per export.

items.title: Translate a PDF and keep its layout.
items.body: Playground has a new **PDF Translation** page. Only the text changes. Images, graphics, backgrounds, tables and form fields stay exactly as they were.

items.title: Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and other Indian scripts render correctly,
items.body: and so do Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Cyrillic and Greek. Chinese, Japanese and Korean aren't supported yet. You'll see a clear message up front, not a broken file.

items.title: Side-by-side preview.
items.body: The original and the translation scroll together page by page, and selecting a segment jumps to its page.

items.title: Overflow flags.
items.body: When a translation is too long for its box, the text is shrunk to fit first. Anything that still doesn't fit is flagged on its segment so a translator can shorten it. No text is ever dropped.

items.title: Also in Cosmos.
items.body: Workflows have a new **PDF Translation** step.

items.title: Pick a Drive folder and translate everything in it.
items.body: In "Choose from Assets", tick a folder instead of files. Every matching file is translated into each language you choose.

items.title: See it before you run it.
items.body: A preview shows every file it will translate with its word count, every file it will skip and why, and the credit cost.

items.title: Output lands next to the source
items.body: in a `{folder} (translated)` folder, in the layout your i18n setup expects:

children.body: Or the language in the file name: `emails/welcome.hi.json`

items.title: Skip what you don't need
items.body: with patterns like `**/fixtures/**` or `config*.json`.

items.title: Supported formats.
items.body: Translate into up to 10 languages per run, from:

items.title: Several languages at once in Text Translation.
items.body: Choose more than one target language, and each gets its own tab of results.

items.title: Open a folder to see what's in it.
items.body: Click a folder card to see every process filed in it, across Translate Video, Translate Photo, Playground, QC and Cosmos, with a tab and count for each.
Open any process from the list. You can also move it to another folder, remove it from the folder or delete it, depending on your permissions.

sections.title: Save to Assets: choose the folder

items.title: "Save to Assets" now asks where to save.
items.body: It opens on the usual default folder, so confirming without changing anything saves where it always did. This works in:

children.body: Quick Create and Image Creator, for one creation or a whole selection

items.title: Upload straight from the picker.
items.body: New files go into the folder you're viewing and come back already selected.

items.title: Preview an export before downloading it.
items.body: Each row in export History has a **Preview** button that plays the finished video.

items.title: Downloads are named properly:
items.body: `{Process name} - Hindi (India).mp4`. The same goes for audio and subtitle files, and names in Hindi, Tamil and other non-Latin scripts now download intact.

items.title: Choose the lip-sync model for each export.
items.body: In **Settings → Provider Preferences**, lip-sync is now a list of providers (Sync.so, Fal), the same as text-to-speech. When more than one model is available, the export panel lets you pick one for that export.

items.title: QE picks up new languages.
items.body: A language added in the editor now appears in the QE panel right away.

items.title: Retry a failed image translation in place.
items.body: It reruns only the step that failed, adds no new version and charges you once.

items.title: Use a whole folder of images
items.body: as sources in Image Translation. It tells you about anything it had to leave out.

items.title: Tell the AI what a memory is for.
items.body: A VitraTM memory now has a **Context** field of up to 1,000 characters describing what it's for, and every AI translation, review pass and QE report for that memory uses it. It's required when you create a memory, and you can change it later from the **Context** button on the memory's page.

items.title: VitraTM settings.
items.body: **Settings → Translation Memory** has a VitraTM card where you can switch the AI review pass on or off and pick a translation mode.

children.body: **Auto** picks the mode for each job.
**Batch**: background translation jobs and QE reports run in the lower-cost batch mode. Instant translations are unaffected.

items.title: Readable QE reports for Word and PowerPoint.
items.body: The report no longer shows formatting markers in the source, translation or suggestions.

items.title: Any playback speed
items.body: in Playground text-to-speech: type a value like 1.35x, and "Apply to all" uses it.

items.title: Draft text-to-speech sessions
items.body: now appear in the process list and can be reopened.

items.title: Breadcrumbs
items.body: on the Brand Kit and Image Creator pages.

items.title: PDF translation: 0.5 credits per source word,
items.body: the same as the other document formats.
